ti: the judge meter is not tamper-evident: an agent that bypasses the shim or rewrites the log scores as cheap instead of disqualified

note: design refinement over the recorded direction, stated: sequence numbers derived from the line count detect mid-file deletion and resets but NOT tail truncation (remaining lines stay contiguous and the next append continues cleanly) — the journal write-event delta is the check that catches tail truncation, because erased calls still wrote their events; prep therefore records a journal-line baseline sidecar, and the two checks together with the per-line nonce cover the three tamper shapes U2 could have used

the meter is now tamper-evident with three measured checks and a DISQUALIFIED verdict labeled apart from invalid in report and aggregate (the gate fails on both, the remedies differ). Per-line sequence numbers catch mid-file deletion and resets; a crypto-random nonce embedded in the shim and echoed per line catches a regenerated log — U2s actual tamper shape; and the journal write-event delta catches tail truncation and shim bypass, which contiguity cannot see because remaining lines stay contiguous under the true nonce while the erased calls still wrote their events. The journal bound is measured, not assumed: the first draft used delta greater than metered calls and immediately disqualified an honest run, because one call writes up to three events (escalation: the move, the side-step, the minted decision; archive skip: two) — the shipped bound is write-capable exit-0 calls times three, with the per-call measurement table in the code comment. Prep records a journal baseline so seeded events stay out of the bound. Tests drive all three tamper shapes against a really-prepped workspace plus the honest-run control; the argv tool index (call -root dir TOOL) cost one red iteration. Live exercise of the hardened shim comes free with the next judge batch

ti: give the judge harness the real tool descriptions so the 20KB schema surface has a measurable benefit side
the bench per-call total is not byte-reproducible across runs, so the reproducibility assertion I shipped in v0.9.0 flakes CI

note: my own flaky assertion, blocking CI

Removed a false invariant I shipped in v0.9.0 and replaced it with a true one. The assertion claimed two Run calls must meter byte-identical per-call totals; they must not, because each Run mints fresh record IDs and the adaptive shortener picks a prefix width from what is unambiguous in that workspace, so two runs can render IDs of different widths. It passed locally on repeated runs and failed on a loaded CI runner at 4162B versus 4168B, blocking an unrelated archive.

It also never pinned what it claimed. Its stated purpose was to prove the schema metering does not perturb the fixture it measures, and a verifier had already shown by mutation that comparing two Runs cannot detect that, since each Run builds its own fixture - the real protection is the signature, schemaBytes taking no workspace root. So it asserted a property the program does not have, in service of a guarantee it could not check.

Replaced with the property that IS stable: schema and manifest sizes must not wander between runs, because unlike the per-call total they carry no record IDs. That is a real invariant and it would catch genuine metering instability.

WORTH RECORDING as the mirror of this session other findings. Those were assertions that looked like coverage and caught nothing. This one caught something real - a genuine difference between two runs - and was WRONG to, because the difference is legitimate. Both come from writing an assertion without first measuring whether the property holds. RECMERGE-003 says prove a fix by mutation; the converse is equally cheap and I skipped it: before asserting an invariant, run it twice.

C1 REAL: 8x local Run()+30x in full-suite runs never showed Bytes variance (too fast to hit same-ms ID collision locally), but mechanism is real+documented: ids.go MinRecordPrefixLen=13 covers 48-bit ts+15 random bits, same-ms pair collides p=2^-15, forcing adaptive width growth -> explains CI 4162B/4168B. SchemaBytes/ManifestBytes stable across all runs. C2 MEANINGFUL: mutated SchemaBytes+=counter -> test correctly FAILED (schema 20024/20025, exit=1); reverted, diff clean vs HEAD, rebuilt green. C3 STABLE: 3x fresh -count=1 runs green (~108s ea); package + this test also green under 12-core yes-loop CPU load (40s/173s). C5: go test ./... exit=0 all pkgs, known flaky tests not hit; go vet clean; gofmt -l internal/ empty. C4: only internal/bench/bench_test.go changed, test-only (confirmed, see waiver). Nit: stale doc comment ~line724 still describes old reproducibility rationale; cosmetic only.
wv: testonly:- NOT a false positive -- confirmed TRUE via git show --stat 944642b (only internal/bench/bench_test.go changed). Waived because test-only is the expected/intended shape of this fix, per task.

note: smallest complete unit available; a comment describing an assertion that no longer exists

Replaced the sentence describing a removed assertion with what the test now does. The old text said the reproducibility assertion below is kept because it is cheap and pins that the scripted total does not wander between runs. That assertion had been deleted, and the property it claimed is false: each Run mints fresh record IDs and a same-millisecond pair can need a longer disambiguating prefix, which shifts rendered totals - it passed about thirty local runs and failed on a loaded CI runner at 4162B versus 4168B, blocking an unrelated archive. The comment now says that, and says what remains asserts instead: the schema and manifest sizes, which carry no record IDs because schemaBytes uses its own throwaway root and the manifest is static text, and which a verifier already mutation-checked by making SchemaBytes vary between calls.

Checked the whole comment against the test body rather than only the flagged sentence, which is what the record VERIFY block asked for: every remaining claim now describes code that exists. Suite exit 0 asserted by capturing the code. Comment-only, no behavior change.

The reason this was worth a record rather than a silent edit: it is the fourth comment in one week found asserting something untrue, after the truncation-marker ordering claim, the schemas-exceed-64KB claim, and the two parser doc comments that said Escalate writes outcome=. The pattern is that comments get edited when the code they sit above changes and NOT when code they merely refer to is deleted - which is the cheaper half of RECMERGE-003 and the one no gate catches.
